fellowship.projectTitle: Open-Source Computational Frameworks for Multi-Omics Analysis of Tumor Heterogeneity and Epigenetic Alterations
fellowship.projectAbstract: The Computational Multidata Junction in Medicine (CMJM) Lab led by Prof. Mei-Ju May Chen focuses on computational multi-omics data analysis, and AI-enabled multi-omics integration to address fundamental and translational questions in precision medicine, with a particular emphasis on cancer and public health. The proposed research theme centers on the development and application of open-source computational frameworks, QuoTHiC, Oncolabe, and methLOY (A machine learning project for predicting LOY status from EPIC array data), in collaboration with the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) for systematic analysis of tumor heterogeneity and epigenetic alterations from large-scale bulk or single-cell sequencing data.
